description: I'm Irina, a civil engineering student. I enjoy applying technical analysis, problem-solving, and development tools (like Python and PyCharm) to hands-on projects and interdisciplinary challenges.
summary:
For those who investigate the evolution of fire and those who combat its consequences on the ground, understanding wildfires requires connecting the past with the immediate future. With this purpose, PyroChronos was born: an interactive geospatial observatory that harmonizes 25 years of thermal records from the MODIS and VIIRS satellites, bridging technological gaps between sensors through regional biome calibration.

Through an interactive globe, a continuous thermal calendar, and local tactical maps, any user can explore the planet's historical footprint or activate a 24-, 48-, and 72-hour predictive simulator. Integrating real meteorology, thermodynamics, and wind vectors, the platform delineates zones with a high probability of expansion versus areas of lower risk, even allowing users to test hypothetical temperature and wind gust scenarios.

By making satellite science accessible to everyone, PyroChronos transforms complex data into clear decisions to protect our ecosystems and support those on the front lines of defense.
details:
PyroChronos is an interactive geospatial observatory and wildfire risk simulator designed to connect 26 years of satellite records with short-term operational predictions. It’s core capabilities include:

  • Harmonized Historical Exploration (2001–2026): Continuous visualization of thermal records from MODIS and VIIRS satellites without technological biases.
  • 3D Planetary Visualization: Interactive globe for global and continental analysis of fire dynamics.
  • Continuous Thermal Calendar (365/366 days): Annual histogram with animated playback and extreme statistical anomaly filters (>P90).
  • Local Tactical Maps (2D and 3D): High-resolution viewers with volumetric grids for detailed field inspection.
  • Predictive Engine (24h, 48h, and 72h): Automated calculation of ignition probability and fire front spread velocity.
  • Interactive What-If Simulator: Sliders to test scenarios by modifying temperature (T) and wind gust (V) real-time values.
  • Exportation and Operational Reports: Structured CSV downloads and instant generation of operational reports.
  • Multilingual Support (EN / ES / PT): Interface available in English, Spanish, and Portuguese, instantly switchable via three selection buttons located in the top-right corner.

How Each Component of the Platform Works

  • Historical Exploration and Harmonization: To unify two and a half decades of satellite data without distortions caused by technological shifts, the platform applies a regional biome model (M'=Mkb) calibrated using the orbital overlap period (2012–2023) between MODIS (1 km) and VIIRS (375 m) sensors. Correction factors kb range from 2.40 in African savannas to 3.10 in boreal and chaparral ecosystems, eliminating sub-pixel sensitivity discrepancies.
  • Planetary Visualization and Thermal Calendar: The global interface runs on a GPU-accelerated engine (Globe.gl / Three.js). The thermal calendar maps every day of the year into a seasonal heatmap format, allowing users to toggle between a general view, the isolated display of anomalies exceeding the 90th percentile, or Real-Time data.
  • Local Tactical Maps: Selecting any risk node or hotspot deploys a specialized viewer (MapLibre GL JS) combining 2D overhead and 3D volumetric views. Within this space, an anisotropic spatial deformation of the fire front is projected, stretching spread cells downwind based on local meteorological vectors.
  • Predictive Engine and What-If Simulator: The calculation backend (predict_engine.py) queries live numerical forecasts from the Open-Meteo NWP API and feeds a multivariable logistic regression model. This calculates ignition probability (Pign) by integrating Vapor Pressure Deficit (VPD via the Tetens equation), soil moisture, and winds. The simulator directly interacts with this model by enabling the dynamic alteration of T and V values to anticipate environmental stress peaks.
  • Exportation and Operational Reports: Designed to streamline communication during critical situations, the system processes active filters to allow both CSV table downloads and the automated drafting of formatted text reports for immediate sharing via emergency channels.

Context, Benefits, and Technology

Beyond its technical features, PyroChronos's fundamental purpose is to restore transparency and scientific rigor to environmental management. By translating complex thermodynamic equations and radiometric data into an intuitive interface that requires no advanced Geographic Information Systems (GIS) background, the platform successfully balances researchers' historical analysis with the tactical utility of first-responder brigades on the front lines, while ensuring smooth navigation even under low connectivity via multilevel caching and climatological backups.

In practice, the platform segments its use cases into three axes: multiannual regime scientific research, tactical planning for forestry brigades, and the deployment of governmental early-warning protocols aimed at mitigating population risk in wildland-urban interface zones.

This entire ecosystem is supported by a robust architecture: a Python 3 backend utilizing Flask, Gunicorn, NumPy, and Pandas to execute analytical processing and expose REST endpoints (/api/data, /api/predict, /api/export-csv), powered by official data sources such as NASA FIRMS (MODIS C6.1 and VIIRS 375m) and Open-Meteo. The frontend relies on HTML5, CSS3, ES6+, Three.js, Globe.gl, and MapLibre GL JS, operating on standard development environments with Git/GitHub version control and Linux deployment.

Future Vision

Looking toward future development, the project's vision aims to expand its operational capabilities through the following evolutionary lines:

  • High-Resolution Topography Integration: Incorporating 30-meter Digital Elevation Models (DEM) from NASA's SRTM mission to model the direct impact of topographic slopes and relief on fire spread-velocity equations.
  • Mass Automated Early-Warning System: Developing a broadcast network inspired by seismic alert systems recently implemented in countries like Colombia and Venezuela, capable of issuing automated preventive notifications ahead of critical ignition windows.
  • Navigation and Travel Platform Integration: Establishing data exchange channels with Google Maps or other mapping services to alert travelers in real time about active fires.
